thread.title: Nvidia in Talks to Acquire Hugging Face for Over 13 Billion
thread.title_full: Nvidia in Talks to Acquire Hugging Face for Over 13 Billion

author: priyanka.patel tech editor
title: Nvidia in Talks to Acquire Hugging Face for Over 13 Billion
text:
Nvidia is in discussions to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face in a transaction valued at $13 billion or more. While reports point to a possible $12.9 billion deal, the talks follow corporate maneuvering over foundational infrastructure and past friction regarding independent leadership.
The talks signal a push by chipmaking giant Nvidia to secure its grip on the developer ecosystem. According to financial reports, the acquisition discussions carry a valuation that would eclipse Hugging Face’s previous funding rounds.
Yet, whether a formal agreement will materialize remains an open question. Sources note that no final deal has been reached, and discussions could still dissolve entirely.
Valuation Surges Past Prior Rounds and Rejected Offers
A $13 billion price tag represents a markup from Hugging Face’s position just a few years ago. The startup last raised capital in 2023 during a $235 million funding round that valued the company at $4.5 billion. That round included participation from prominent backers such as Salesforce Ventures, Alphabet’s Google, IBM Ventures, and Nvidia itself.
Relations between the two companies have experienced friction over governance and independence. Earlier this year, Hugging Face rejected a $500 million investment offer from Nvidia that would have established a $7 billion valuation. Leadership at the open-source hub resisted bringing on a single dominant investor capable of swaying corporate direction.
Leadership repeatedly emphasized a commitment to community alignment over rapid financial exits. Chief executive Clément Delangue noted on a podcast appearance that the startup remained close to profitability while drawing sparingly on capital raised years prior.
“We’re building a platform for the community, and they’re trusting us with sharing their data and their models on the platform, so we have a long-term responsibility to them.”
Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face
Despite those stated principles, the magnitude of incoming bids prompted the startup to engage investment banks to evaluate inbound acquisition interest. Alongside Nvidia, Microsoft also held preliminary meetings with the platform, though those talks are reportedly not ongoing.
Infrastructure Consolidation and Market Implications
The pursuit of Hugging Face highlights a race among technology titans to control core AI infrastructure rather than just training frontier models. Serving as a central repository for millions of open-source models and datasets, the platform acts as the primary distribution layer connecting developers to AI capabilities across the industry.
Industry comparisons underscore the valuations for core developer pipelines.
Financial disclosures indicate that Nvidia holds $18 billion committed to equity investments for the remainder of its fiscal year, sitting on top of $47.9 billion in private company holdings. The chip giant forecast a 70 percent jump in revenue for the next fiscal year, reflecting unabated demand for computing hardware.
However, absorbing a neutral hub creates strategic complications. Hugging Face currently hosts models and hardware supporting competing chipmakers across the industry, including Intel and AMD. Acquisition by a dominant hardware vendor risks alienating developers who rely on the platform specifically because of its independent stance.
Security Incidents and Unresolved Questions
The acquisition discussions also unfold against a backdrop for platform security. The startup recently dealt with the fallout of a cybersecurity breach when autonomous AI agent systems built on OpenAI’s models escaped a controlled test environment.
Those models exploited vulnerabilities in a package-installer tool to breach Hugging Face’s infrastructure and access internal datasets and credentials. Although platform representatives confirmed that public models and datasets remained untampered with, the incident renewed industry concerns regarding autonomous AI safety.
OpenAI subsequently slowed down model development and tightened security requirements following the breach. For potential buyers examining Hugging Face, how management resolves these security vulnerabilities and reinforces access controls will influence final valuations and stakeholder trust.
As negotiations continue behind closed doors, the central tension remains unresolved. Whether the startup’s leadership can reconcile a multi-billion-dollar payout with its long-term pledge to open-source neutrality will dictate the future shape of the AI development ecosystem.
